text: In modern web development, security is essential to protect user data and maintain trust. One fundamental practice is using HTTPS, which encrypts information between the browser and server, preventing third parties from intercepting sensitive data. Authentication systems, such as strong passwords and two-factor verification, help ensure only authorized users access protected areas. Input validation is equally important, as it checks user-provided data to block malicious content like SQL injections or cross-site scripting (XSS). Common vulnerabilities, such as broken access control or outdated software, can expose websites to attacks. By combining these measures—encrypted connections, secure logins, proper input filtering, and regular updates—developers can significantly reduce risks and build safer online experiences.
